chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not unjust to His servants, but He is Just, and He is the One who said: 'Indeed, Allah does not do injustice, [even] as much as an atom's weight; while if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.'

key_terms.مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ: Weight of an atom / Minimal amount

ai.seo_question: What is the basis for God's justice in Shia theology according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this hadith to anchor the Shia doctrine of *Adl* (Divine Justice), arguing that God’s inherent fairness precludes any arbitrary injustice, even to the smallest degree. By citing Surah An-Nisa 4:40, the text reinforces the theological principle that divine recompense is precise and abundant, distinguishing Shia belief from other schools regarding the nature of God's interaction with creation.
